s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scrotal swelling with acute worsening and a palpable testicular mass
salient_findings: Firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on ultrasound
key_facts: 20-year history of left testicular bloating and dull pain
Acute worsening of symptoms over the past 10 days
Left testis is enlarged, firm, and smooth
Transillumination of the left testis is negative
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound shows a hypoechoic lesion in the left testis
The lesion has internal blood flow on ultrasound
Bilateral epididymal cysts are present
A small left hydrocele is present
Serum CA19-9 level is elevated at 57.5 U/mL
Alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers are within normal limits

differentials: Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis
per_call: Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common testicular cancer, matches ultrasound findings of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA19-9 level and acute worsening of symptoms suggest aggressive testicular cancer, which is consistent with non-seminomatous germ cell tumor

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm and smooth testis on examination, along with a long history of testicular bloating, could be indicative of testicular lymphoma

shortlist.label: Testicular teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound findings of a hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow could be consistent with a teratoma, although less likely given the patient's age and symptom progression

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA19-9 level and aggressive symptom progression could be indicative of embryonal carcinoma, a subtype of non-seminomatous germ cell tumor

raw.rationale: Elevated CA19-9 level and presence of a hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow in the left testis, along with a 20-year history of testicular bloating and dull pain, are more indicative of a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, which can present with elevated tumor markers and complex ultrasound findings

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with elevated human chorionic gonadotropin and has a more uniform ultrasound appearance

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Usually occurs in older men and is less likely to present with a hypoechoic lesion and elevated CA19-9

rejected.label: Testicular teratoma
rejected.why: May contain elements from all three germ layers, but the clinical presentation and ultrasound findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: A subtype of non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, but the provided information does not specifically point to this diagnosis over the broader category
